subject: Applied Thermodynamics
summary: reciprocating air compressors (clearance, volumetric efficiency, multi-staging and intercooling), the Rankine cycle with superheat, reheat and regenerative feed heating, and the Brayton gas turbine cycle with component efficiencies, regeneration, intercooling and combined cycles

questions.text: The Carnot cycle is not used as the practical model for steam power plants mainly because
opts: its efficiency is lower than that of the Rankine cycle
it would require compressing a wet (two-phase) mixture in the pump and expanding very wet steam in the turbine
it needs a condenser
it cannot use superheated steam at all
questions.ans: (B) it would require compressing a wet (two-phase) mixture in the pump and expanding very wet steam in the turbine
solution: Concept: A Carnot vapour cycle adds and rejects heat isothermally inside the wet region.
Its compression would start from a wet mixture: a two-phase compressor is impractical and absorbs large work.
Its expansion ends with very wet steam, which erodes turbine blades. The Rankine cycle condenses fully and pumps liquid instead: (B).
Exam tip: Carnot efficiency is the upper limit; the Rankine cycle trades a little efficiency for practicality.

questions.text: In a simple Rankine cycle the steam enters the turbine at 8 MPa with h<sub>1</sub> = 3230 kJ/kg and leaves the isentropic turbine at 10 kPa with h<sub>2</sub> = 2140 kJ/kg. Saturated liquid leaves the condenser with h<sub>3</sub> = 192 kJ/kg and v = 0.00101 m³/kg. The cycle efficiency (in %, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: η = (wT − wP)/qin, with the pump work wP = v(pboiler − pcond).
w<sub>T</sub> = 3230 − 2140 = 1090 kJ/kg; w<sub>net</sub> = 1081.93 kJ/kg
Exam tip: Here the pump work is only 0.7 % of the turbine work; neglecting it changes η by about 0.1 %.

questions.text: In a Rankine cycle the boiler pressure is raised, keeping the maximum steam temperature and the condenser pressure unchanged. Then
opts: the efficiency falls and the exhaust becomes drier
both the efficiency and the exhaust dryness increase
the efficiency rises but the steam at the turbine exhaust becomes wetter
neither changes
questions.ans: (C) the efficiency rises but the steam at the turbine exhaust becomes wetter
solution: Concept: Efficiency depends on the mean temperature of heat addition.
Higher boiler pressure raises the saturation temperature, so the mean temperature of heat addition rises and η increases.
But at the same maximum temperature the expansion line shifts to lower entropy, ending deeper in the wet region: wetter exhaust (C).
Exam tip: This is exactly why reheat is used with high boiler pressures.

questions.text: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg·K) at 1 bar and 300 K is compressed to 9 bar in a two-stage reciprocating compressor with perfect intercooling and the optimum intermediate pressure. Compression follows pV¹·³ = constant in both stages. The minimum total work per kg of air (in kJ/kg, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: With perfect intercooling (back to T1) and p2 = √(p1p3), both stages do equal work: W = 2[n/(n − 1)]RT1[(p3/p1)(n−1)/(2n) − 1].
p<sub>2</sub> = √9 = 3 bar; each stage has a ratio of 3; (n − 1)/n = 0.2308
Exam tip: Single-stage compression to 9 bar would need 4.333 × 86.1 × (90.2308 − 1) = 246.4 kJ/kg: intercooling saves about 13 %.

questions.text: The volumetric efficiency of a single-stage reciprocating air compressor with a fixed clearance volume
opts: increases as the delivery pressure increases
is independent of the pressure ratio
is 100 % whenever the compression is isothermal
decreases as the pressure ratio increases
questions.ans: (D) decreases as the pressure ratio increases
solution: Concept: ηv = 1 + C − C(p2/p1)1/n.
The clearance air re-expands to a larger volume when the pressure ratio is larger, so less fresh air is drawn in.
Hence ηv decreases with pressure ratio (D) and becomes zero at the limiting ratio (1 + 1/C)n.
Exam tip: This is the second reason (besides work saving) for multi-stage compression at high pressure ratios.

questions.text: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg·K, γ = 1.4) at 300 K is compressed from 1 bar to 6 bar in a steady-flow compressor. The isothermal efficiency, defined as (isothermal work)/(isentropic work) for the same pressure ratio (in %, round off to two decimal places), is ______
solution: Concept: Isothermal work = RT1 ln r; isentropic work = [γ/(γ − 1)]RT1(r(γ−1)/γ − 1).
Exam tip: RT1 cancels, so the ratio depends only on the pressure ratio and γ.

questions.text: The thermal efficiency of an ideal (air-standard) Brayton cycle depends on
opts: the pressure ratio only (for a given γ)
the maximum temperature only
both the maximum and minimum temperatures
the mass flow rate of air
questions.ans: (A) the pressure ratio only (for a given γ)
solution: Concept: η = 1 − 1/rp(γ−1)/γ = 1 − T1/T2.
Neither Tmax nor the flow rate appears: (A).
The turbine inlet temperature does, however, decide the net work per kg (and the optimum pressure ratio).
Exam tip: With component inefficiencies, η also depends on T3/T1: a hotter turbine inlet then helps efficiency too.

questions.text: An ideal Brayton cycle works on air (c<sub>p</sub> = 1.005 kJ/kg·K, γ = 1.4) with a compressor inlet temperature of 300 K, a pressure ratio of 8 and a turbine inlet temperature of 1300 K. The back work ratio (compressor work/turbine work, round off to three decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Back work ratio = wC/wT = (T2 − T1)/(T3 − T4).
Shortcut: since T<sub>2</sub>/T<sub>1</sub> = T<sub>3</sub>/T<sub>4</sub>, BWR = T<sub>2</sub>/T<sub>3</sub> = 543.4/1300.
Exam tip: Gas turbines spend 40–60 % of turbine work on the compressor; a steam plant spends about 1 %.

questions.text: The T–s diagram shows an ideal Brayton cycle 1–2–3–4 with an ideal regenerator, in which the compressed air (2 → x) is heated by the turbine exhaust (4 → y). For fixed T<sub>1</sub> and T<sub>3</sub>, the thermal efficiency of this cycle
opts: increases as the pressure ratio increases
decreases as the pressure ratio increases
is independent of the pressure ratio
equals the Carnot efficiency at every pressure ratio
questions.ans: (B) decreases as the pressure ratio increases
solution: Concept: For an ideal regenerative Brayton cycle, η = 1 − (T1/T3)rp(γ−1)/γ.
As rp rises, T4 falls towards T2 and less heat can be recovered, so η decreases (B).
At r<sub>p</sub> → 1 it tends to the Carnot value 1 − T<sub>1</sub>/T<sub>3</sub> (but with zero net work).
Exam tip: This is the opposite trend to the simple Brayton cycle, whose efficiency rises with rp.

questions.text: A gas turbine plant works on air (c<sub>p</sub> = 1.005 kJ/kg·K, γ = 1.4). Air enters the compressor at 290 K; the pressure ratio is 6 and the turbine inlet temperature is 1100 K. The isentropic efficiencies of the compressor and turbine are 0.82 and 0.88. The thermal efficiency of the plant (in %, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Find the actual exit temperatures from the isentropic efficiencies, then η = wnet/qin.
Exam tip: Component losses hit gas turbines hard because the net work is a small difference of two large works.

questions.text: Compared with a closed feed-water heater, an open (direct-contact) feed-water heater
opts: needs a separate pump after it to raise the feed water to the next pressure
cannot be used for deaeration
keeps the bled steam and feed water separate
is always more expensive
questions.ans: (A) needs a separate pump after it to raise the feed water to the next pressure
solution: Concept: In an open heater the bled steam mixes with the feed water at the bleed pressure.
The mixture leaves as saturated liquid at that (lower) pressure, so a pump is required after each open heater (A).
Open heaters are cheap, give good heat transfer and also remove dissolved gases (deaerator).
Exam tip: Closed heaters keep the streams apart (a shell-and-tube exchanger), so only one feed pump is needed.

questions.text: A steam power plant has a net work output of 1125 kJ/kg of steam and receives 3000 kJ/kg of heat in the boiler. Its heat rate (in kJ/kWh) is ______
solution: Concept: Heat rate = heat supplied per kWh of net work = 3600/η kJ/kWh.
Heat rate = 3600/0.375 = 9600 kJ/kWh
Exam tip: The lower the heat rate, the better the plant; the steam rate 3600/wnet = 3.2 kg/kWh is a different measure.

questions.text: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg·K) at 1 bar and 300 K is compressed to 27 bar in a three-stage reciprocating compressor with perfect intercooling and optimum stage pressures. Compression follows pV¹·²⁵ = constant. The minimum total work per kg of air (in kJ/kg, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: For N stages with perfect intercooling the optimum stage ratio is (pfinal/p1)1/N and W = N[n/(n − 1)]RT1[rs(n−1)/n − 1].
r<sub>s</sub> = 27<sup>1/3</sup> = 3 (stage pressures 1, 3, 9, 27 bar); (n − 1)/n = 0.2
Exam tip: Each stage does equal work and has equal delivery temperature (300 × 1.2457 = 373.7 K).

questions.text: In a combined gas turbine–steam turbine power plant,
opts: the steam cycle is the topping cycle and the gas turbine the bottoming cycle
the gas turbine is the topping cycle and its exhaust raises steam for the bottoming Rankine cycle
the two cycles share the same working fluid
the overall efficiency is the product of the two cycle efficiencies
questions.ans: (B) the gas turbine is the topping cycle and its exhaust raises steam for the bottoming Rankine cycle
solution: Concept: The gas turbine works at high temperature and rejects heat at 450–600 °C, ideal for raising steam.
So the gas turbine is the topping cycle (B) and a heat-recovery steam generator feeds the Rankine bottoming cycle.
η<sub>overall</sub> = η<sub>1</sub> + η<sub>2</sub> − η<sub>1</sub>η<sub>2</sub>, which exceeds either efficiency.
Exam tip: Modern combined-cycle plants reach about 60 % efficiency.

questions.text: A gas turbine cycle uses many stages of intercooling and of reheating together with an ideal regenerator. As the number of stages tends to infinity, its efficiency approaches that of the
opts: Otto cycle
Diesel cycle
Rankine cycle
Ericsson cycle, which equals the Carnot efficiency between the same temperatures
questions.ans: (D) Ericsson cycle, which equals the Carnot efficiency between the same temperatures
solution: Concept: Infinite intercooling makes compression isothermal at Tmin; infinite reheating makes expansion isothermal at Tmax.
With an ideal regenerator handling the constant-pressure processes, all external heat is exchanged at T<sub>max</sub> and T<sub>min</sub>.
That is the Ericsson cycle (D), whose efficiency is 1 − Tmin/Tmax.
Exam tip: In practice two or three stages give most of the gain.
